context.why: Stories 1 and 2 are accepted. fairdm/api/serializers.py has OrganizationListSerializer (url, html_url, uuid, name, type, country, identifiers) and, as the pattern to follow, PersonListSerializer and PersonSerializer. fairdm/api/viewsets.py has OrganizationViewSet serving the list serializer for the single record too, and PersonViewSet with get_serializer_class(). fairdm/api/filters.py has PersonFilterSet and IdentifierFilter. This story gives a single organization its fuller serializer, adds the organization filters, and documents both, mirroring what story 2 did for people. The moved test TestContributor.test_an_organisation_is_returned_with_what_its_profile_page_shows lost its assertions on the parent in story 1 (decisions.md D14): T015 asserts them on the single record.
spec_sections: Edge Cases (an organization that is its own top level)
prior_decisions: OrganizationSerializer(OrganizationListSerializer) adds exactly: alternative_names, profile, city, links, image, parent, sub_organizations, members. Do NOT add `projects` or `datasets`; story 4 adds them. Do not add added, modified, lat, lon, location, synced_data, config or owner.
`links`: the same shape PersonSerializer gives (a list of addresses). `parent` is {uuid, url, name} from OrganizationReferenceSerializer or null. `sub_organizations` is a list of the same, by name.

`members`: one entry per affiliation to the organization whose type is at least Affiliation.MembershipType.MEMBER and whose end_date is null, the people who run it first then by name (the order Organization.get_current_memberships() gives). Each entry is exactly {person: {uuid, url, name}, type} with type the lower-case name of the membership type (member, admin, owner), the same wording PersonSerializer uses for an affiliation's type; reuse that code, do not write it twice. A member who is a superuser or the anonymous account is left out: use RecordReferenceField.hidden_contributor_pks(context) or filter the prefetch with Person.objects.real().

Query count (T017, FR-024): Organization.get_current_memberships() runs its own query and prefetches things this serializer does not need, so do not call it per organization. Prefetch on OrganizationViewSet's queryset instead: a Prefetch of `affiliations` filtered to current verified ones with select_related('person'), plus `sub_organizations` and select_related('parent'). The list action must not pay for the members prefetch if that is simple to arrange in get_queryset(); the list query count test from story 1 (TestQueryCount's organizations kind) must stay green either way. A person reference needs the person's uuid, name and the people route only, so no further query per member.

OrganizationFilterSet in fairdm/api/filters.py: `type` (the stored code), `country` (the two-letter code), `parent` (ModelChoiceFilter by uuid, to_field_name='uuid'; a database number is refused with a 400), `top_level` (BooleanFilter: true gives organizations with no parent, false gives those with one) and `identifier` (the existing IdentifierFilter). Set it as OrganizationViewSet.filterset_class as PersonViewSet does with its own.
OrganizationViewSet.get_serializer_class() returns OrganizationListSerializer for the list action and OrganizationSerializer otherwise.

T019: mirror story 2's schema tests in tests/test_api/test_schema.py for organizations (the list component and the single component list their own fields; the list operation documents type, country, parent, top_level and identifier). In docs/portal-development/restful-api.md extend the short Organizations section with the single organization's fields in a table, what the list leaves out, the filters with one example request each, and that only current verified members are listed. Name OrganizationSerializer and OrganizationFilterSet, and any other new public class, in the page.
The story 2 implementer noted that the documentation generator cannot guess the type of a ModelChoiceFilter by uuid and defaults to string. That is acceptable; do not add machinery for it.
Formatting: do not run a formatter over files you are not editing. tests/ is excluded from the pre-commit hooks; run `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format` only on the test files you edit.
